subject.title: refactor(prompt): use plain inbound context labels and drop system-tag sanitizer

question: Should this cleanup preserve centralized neutralization of nested system-style lines at the system-event queue/render boundary, or is there an approved invariant proving every enqueue caller independently isolates every external line before it reaches a prompt?
rationale: The branch deliberately removes a shared security normalization primitive across several ingress paths, while the demonstrated hook-name normalization is not a complete substitute for the generic queue contract.

options.title: Restore the shared queue boundary
options.body: Keep the plain inbound-context marker refactor, but retain or replace the queue-wide normalization with coverage for multiline node, hook, and plugin-originated events.

options.title: Approve a new rendering invariant
options.body: Accept sanitizer removal only after documenting and testing a single renderer that prefixes or isolates every queued event line regardless of origin.

options.title: Pause the sanitizer removal
options.body: Land only the label and SDK compatibility work while retaining the existing system-event defense until the cross-caller security contract is settled.

recommendation.title: Restore the shared queue boundary
recommendation.body: Keep the plain inbound-context marker refactor, but retain or replace the queue-wide normalization with coverage for multiline node, hook, and plugin-originated events.

likelyOwner.reason: The current branch owns the affected cleanup and contains the proposed replacement controls, although broader security-boundary ownership should be confirmed by a repository owner.
